findings.element: Run reconciliation error when a required upload is missing (Assisted, two drop zones)
findings.finding: When a required file is missing, the blocked Run shows the generic 'Upload the required file' and moves focus to the Run button. It does not say which of the two upload zones is empty or mark that zone.
findings.user_impact: A first-time user facing two 'Upload file *' zones on the create screen, where the funnel already loses most users, has to work out which file is missing. In the upload branch the error is a near dead end, unlike the field errors fixed in round 1.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the missing file in the error (for example 'Upload the Payouts report from Stripe'), mark that drop zone invalid, and scroll it into view.

evidence.action: Stripe + clearing, Set import methods (Integration side Assisted), uploaded one of the two files, clicked Run reconciliation
evidence.observed: error "Upload the required file"; focus moved to button#run "Run reconciliation"; no zone was identified

findings.finding: Custom ranges that are entirely in the future, or that end today, are accepted and the run starts. The inputs have no min or max, although the domain rule says today's date cannot be selected.
findings.user_impact: The user starts a run for a period with no settled data, or one that includes today. They wait for a run that cannot produce a meaningful result, and it may block a later valid run for the same clearing account.
findings.suggested_fix: Cap the end date at yesterday and refuse ranges that start in the future, with an inline message next to the date inputs.

evidence.action: Stripe + clearing, Date range = Custom, entered Nov 1–30 and then Sep 1–25 (today), clicked Run
evidence.observed: future-only Nov 1–30: error "", started=true; range ending today Sep 1–25: error "", started=true; input min="" max=""

findings.element: How we get the data > Integration side Upload file for Stripe non-clearing accounts ('How to get this file')
findings.finding: When a Stripe non-clearing account forces Manual, the Stripe upload is labelled only 'How to get this file'. It never names the report to export, while the Assisted path names 'Balance change from the activity' and 'Payouts'.
findings.user_impact: A first-time user who picks an account like Stripe fees or Business Checking is asked for a Stripe file without being told which one. This is likely to stall them or lead to the wrong export.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the required Stripe report in the Manual upload label and accordion, as the Assisted and QuickBooks uploads already do.

evidence.action: Integration = mzkt.by (Stripe), Account = Stripe fees (and again with Business Checking)
evidence.observed: Integration side shows "Import method * Manual / Upload file * / How to get this file", while the QuickBooks side reads "How to get General ledger export from QuickBooks Online"

findings.element: How we get the data > 'Set import methods' toggle link on the automatic retrieval card
findings.finding: Clicking 'Set import methods' does more than reveal settings. It switches the Integration side from zero uploads to Assisted with two required uploads, even though the clearing account supports Automated.
findings.user_impact: A first-time user who opens the link to see what automatic retrieval does ends up with two mandatory uploads. If they then click Run, it is blocked by 'Upload the required file'.
findings.suggested_fix: When the link is opened, keep both sides on the current Automated method, so that uploads appear only after the user deliberately picks Assisted or Manual.

evidence.action: Stripe + clearing (automatic card shown, no uploads), clicked 'Set import methods'
evidence.observed: label changed to "Use automatic retrieval"; Integration Import method value = Assisted with two "Upload file *" zones (Balance change from the activity, Payouts); Accounting side stays Automated

findings.element: What to reconcile > Account group 'Synder accounts (manual file upload required)' and the resulting Accounting (QuickBooks) Import method
findings.finding: The same account group gives different requirements depending on the integration. A Stripe account in that group forces QuickBooks to Manual with a General ledger upload, while a PayPal or Shopify account in the same group keeps QuickBooks on Automated.
findings.user_impact: The user cannot predict from the group label how much work an account will need. Stripe users who pick a non-clearing account unexpectedly have to export a QuickBooks general ledger, and PayPal users do not.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the QuickBooks-side behaviour for manual-group accounts the same across integrations, or say in the group label or hint exactly which side needs an upload.

evidence.action: Picked Stripe + Stripe fees, then PayPal + PayPal clearing, then Shopify + Shopify clearing (Synder)
evidence.observed: Stripe fees: Accounting Import method options [Manual] only, with 'General ledger export from QuickBooks Online' upload required. PayPal and Shopify (all accounts in the 'manual file upload required' group): Accounting Import method 'Automated (recommended) / Manual', no QuickBooks upload

gaps: Retrieval failure and empty-result states are not implemented, so it cannot be checked whether a failed sync names the precondition (missing mappings, multi-currency off, closed period, lost QBO authorization) and how to fix it (KF-9).
Overlapping-period validation for the same clearing account was never exercised, so it is unknown whether a conflicting period is caught before Run or only afterwards.
Run was only exercised to success for Stripe + clearing on automatic retrieval. A full run on the Stripe non-clearing, PayPal and Shopify manual paths (all files supplied) was not recorded.
Run with the Accounting side on Manual and its QuickBooks file missing was not recorded, so the error copy and target for that case are unknown.
The Shopify prototype shows Assisted/Manual and puts every Shopify account in the manual group, while the spec lists Automated/Manual. This is a known open question and was not re-flagged here.
